title: Animate on entry, never on scroll position
intent: Pay for motion once when a section arrives instead of paying on every scroll frame.
when_to_use: sections enter the viewport and the entrance is the effect being designed
the page must stay responsive while the user scrolls fast
when_not_to_use: the brief requires a timeline tied to scroll position, which is a different decision with its own frame budget and a complete static first frame
the content must be readable at every scroll position, where an entrance animation would hide text
rules: no window scroll listener drives an animation
an entrance animation runs at most once per element
the animated properties are transform and opacity only
the reduced motion path shows the final state immediately, with no fade and no delay
trade_off: You give up motion that answers the reader's hand continuously, which is what makes a long page feel alive, and the page can read as a set of separate slides.
failure_mode: One observer per element with no shared threshold, so sections animate at inconsistent moments and the page flickers during fast scrolling.

example.brief: Story page with six sections that reveal as the reader advances.
example.ruling: One shared observer with a single threshold triggers a translate and opacity entrance once per section, no scroll listener exists, and reduced motion renders every section already in place.
